title: Debezium: capture committed changes without inventing business meaning
outcome: Explain CDC, snapshots, log positions, outbox routing, and duplicate-safe downstream processing.
useCase: Search/reporting projections and deliberate event publication.
benefits: Captures committed changes without app-level network dual writes.
drawbacks: Connector state, source logs, schema exposure, and cutover require operations.
version: Pinned local examples · version-labelled configuration fragments
cue: Committed change is the source. Business meaning is your contract.

sections.title: Break it and reason about the repair

trace.title: Business transaction
trace.detail: Change data capture reads database changes through a supported source mechanism. Debezium connectors can take an initial snapshot and continue from a log position. This is useful for integration/projections, but a row change is not automatically a well-designed business event.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Initial snapshot → catch-up log position → committed changes → routed records → consumer effects. Restart at the connector’s saved position and expect the selected delivery/recovery contract, including possible repeats.

Trace event_id from outbox row through connector/topic to the consumer inbox. Raw CDC delete/tombstone behavior and business cancellation semantics are different questions.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: CDC may expose columns not intended for downstream systems if schema/filtering is careless. A stopped replication slot/log reader can grow retained WAL. Running both polling and CDC publishers without coordination can duplicate events.
